4th Period.workingNow: Writing week06-mod-design.md — your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic, and state map — and committing it.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: week06-mod-design.md in your Mario repo — your full MDA design (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) for your mod, plus a state map of the one mechanic you build first — committed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can document my mod design so that someone else could read my file and build the same thing I planned.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.19 — Document programs in order to make them easier to follow, test, and debug.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas and information.

4th Period.connections: You designed it Monday and Tuesday, mapped it Wednesday, and touched the real code yesterday. Today it becomes a document someone else could build from. Next week you start building the mod for real, one piece at a time.

6th Period.workingNow: Handing your diagram to a partner and watching them try to get it stuck.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A finished state machine diagram for one thing you choose — at least 5 states, every state with a labeled way in and a labeled way out — partner-tested and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can test my state machine with a partner so that I can find the paths I did not think about.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.11 — Justifying own arguments and evaluating others' arguments in speaking and writing.
agenda: Overview: today you test it (2 min)
I do: how to walk a partner through a machine (8 min)
We do: trace one path as a class (7 min)
You do: partner test, then fix your diagram (25 min)
Exit Ticket: one thing you fixed (5 min)
6th Period.connections: You have five states on paper. Today someone else drives — they pick triggers and you move through your own machine until something breaks. Fix it, and you have a finished state machine. Next week you use it to build a real game with SchoolAI.
